sections.heading: What RA 6713 is and who it covers
sections.body:
**RA 6713** is the "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees" (Section 1). A **code of conduct** is a set of rules on how to behave at work. Section 2 says officials and employees "shall at all times be accountable to the people."

Key definitions (Section 3):

- **Public officials** (3(b)): elected or appointed, "permanent or temporary," career or non-career, "whether or not they receive compensation."
- **Family** (3(g)): "spouses and unmarried children under eighteen (18) years of age."
- **Receiving any gift** (3(d)): even at Christmas, a gift from someone who is not family or a relative counts if its value is not nominal (token-sized), or if it is given for a favor.

Full text: [Lawphil](https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html) or the [Official Gazette](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1989/02/20/republic-act-no-6713/).

sections.heading: The eight norms of conduct (Section 4)
sections.body:
A **norm** is a standard of behaviour. Section 4(A) lists eight. Find the key idea in the story, then match it to these key words:

| Norm | Key words from the law |
| --- | --- |
| (a) Commitment to public interest | public interest "over and above personal interest"; avoid "wastage in public funds" |
| (b) Professionalism | "excellence, professionalism, intelligence and skill" |
| (c) Justness and sincerity | "shall not discriminate against anyone, especially the poor and the underprivileged" |
| (d) Political neutrality | service to everyone "regardless of party affiliation or preference" |
| (e) Responsiveness to the public | "prompt, courteous, and adequate service"; "avoid red tape" |
| (f) Nationalism and patriotism | loyal "to the Republic and to the Filipino people"; "locally produced goods" |
| (g) Commitment to democracy | "supremacy of civilian authority over the military" |
| (h) Simple living | "modest lives appropriate to their positions and income" |

Norm (c) also bars undue favors to relatives, except appointments to "strictly confidential" posts or to coterminous personal staff.

sections.heading: Duties and deadlines (Section 5)
sections.body:
- **Letters** (5(a)): reply "within fifteen (15) working days from receipt." The reply "must contain the action taken on the request."
- **Annual performance report** (5(b)): heads of offices, within 45 working days from the end of the year.
- **Documents** (5(c)): "not more than three (3) signatories," as far as practicable. If a signatory is absent, "the official next-in-rank or officer in charge" signs.

**Counting working days:** skip weekends and holidays. Day 1 is the first working day after the letter arrives. 15 working days is 3 work weeks, so a letter received on a Monday (no holidays) is due on the Monday 3 weeks later.

sections.heading: Prohibited acts (Section 7)
sections.body:
- **(a)** No financial interest "in any transaction requiring the approval of their office."
- **(b)** No job in a private business "regulated, supervised or licensed by their office"; no private practice unless the law allows it and it does not conflict with official work; no recommending anyone to a business with "a regular or pending official transaction with their office." These rules last **one year** after leaving office. Private practice may resume sooner, but not in matters before the old office.
- **(c)** No using confidential information "to further their private interests."
- **(d)** No soliciting or accepting any "gift, gratuity, favor, entertainment, loan or anything of monetary value" linked to the job. From foreign governments, only three kinds are allowed: a souvenir "of nominal value"; a scholarship, fellowship or medical treatment; and travel entirely outside the Philippines, with the head of office's permission.

sections.heading: SALN, divestment and penalties (Sections 8 to 11)
sections.body:
The **SALN** (Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth) is a sworn list of what you own and owe. Honorary officials, laborers and casual or temporary workers are exempt.

| When (Section 8(A)) | Deadline |
| --- | --- |
| Starting | within 30 days after assumption of office |
| Every year | on or before April 30 |
| Leaving | within 30 days after separation |

**Divestment** (Section 9): if a conflict of interest arises, resign from your position in the private business within **30 days** of assuming office "and/or" divest your shares within **60 days**. Do whichever removes the conflict, or both if both cause it.

**Penalties** (Section 11(a)): a fine of up to 6 months' salary, suspension of up to 1 year, or removal. For violating Sections 7, 8 or 9: prison of up to **5 years**, a fine of up to **₱5,000**, or both.

sections.heading: Common traps
sections.body:
- **Working days vs. days.** Letters get 15 *working* days, starting the day after receipt. SALN deadlines are 30 days.
- **Christmas is no excuse.** A gift above nominal value still counts.
- **Family is narrow.** Only the spouse and unmarried children under 18. Parents are not included.
- **Whose money?** Saving government resources is public interest. A modest personal lifestyle is simple living.
- **Swapped numbers.** Resign in 30, divest in 60. Suspension up to 1 year, prison up to 5 years. The first SALN is due 30 days after starting, not on April 30.

glossaryTerms.definition: Under RA 6713, anyone in government service: elected or appointed, permanent or temporary, career or non-career, paid or unpaid.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Public official – lahat ng nasa gobyerno, elected man o appointed, permanent o temporary, may sweldo man o wala

glossaryTerms.definition: A standard of behaviour that public officials and employees must follow at work. Section 4 lists eight.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Norm of conduct – pamantayan ng tamang asal sa trabaho; walo ang nakalista sa Section 4

glossaryTerms.definition: A day the office is open for work. Saturdays, Sundays and holidays are not counted.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Working day – araw na bukas ang opisina; hindi kasama ang Sabado, Linggo at holiday

glossaryTerms.definition: Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth: a sworn list of what a public employee owns and owes.
glossaryTerms.taglish: SALN – listahan ng ari-arian at utang na sinusumpaan ng empleyado ng gobyerno

glossaryTerms.definition: A very small, token value, like a cheap souvenir.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Nominal value – maliit na halaga lang, parang simpleng pasalubong o souvenir

glossaryTerms.definition: When an official's private business could be affected by, or work against, his official duties.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Conflict of interest – kapag nagbabanggaan ang pansariling negosyo at ang tungkulin sa gobyerno

glossaryTerms.definition: Giving up ownership of shares or other interests, to someone who is not a spouse or relative.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Divestment – pagbitaw o paglipat ng shares sa ibang tao na hindi asawa o kamag-anak

glossaryTerms.definition: Ending at the same time. A coterminous staff member's term ends when the official's term ends.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Coterminous – sabay matatapos; tapos ang termino ng staff kapag tapos na ang termino ng opisyal
